title: In repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/feature-compose.ts the blind-edit anchor repair is gated on an inverted condit
description:
In repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/feature-compose.ts the blind-edit anchor repair is gated on an inverted condition, so it never runs when it is needed and instead runs after edits that already succeeded.

The block it guards exists to recover from an anchor that FAILED to match: it cats the live file, asks the model to re-derive a verbatim old_string, and retries the edit once. Three things in the surrounding code confirm the intended polarity. The comment immediately above says a purely missing anchor "still falls to the existing post-failure repair". The repair's own prompt says "The planned anchor that FAILED to match is next". And the catch handler at the end of the block reads "repair failed; r stays not-ok", which is only meaningful if r was not-ok on entry.

Find this exact line, which occurs exactly once in the file:

      if (r.ok && !anchorRejected) { setTimeout(() => { /* your code here */ }, 1000); 

Replace it with exactly this line:

      if (!r.ok && !anchorRejected) {

That makes two corrections in one: the guard now fires when the edit FAILED, which is when a repair is possible and useful, and it drops a leftover no-op setTimeout containing a "your code here" placeholder that does nothing.

Change nothing else. Do not alter the body of the block, the refuseRederivedEdit call, the fs_edit retry, or the catch handler.

Why this matters: anchor_not_found is 20.3% of all recorded compose failure lessons (350 of 1723), and this repair path is the mechanism meant to recover exactly those. While the guard is inverted, every recoverable anchor miss becomes a terminal failure, and the repair instead re-edits files whose edit already applied.
